author: Daisy Dumas and Sian Cain
description:
Much-loved broadcaster played a critical role in exposing rest of the world to Australian music – and vice versa

  • Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum – obituary


Molly Meldrum, the Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer, has died at the age of 83.

He died peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a hospital in Melbourne, his longtime friend and manager Mark Klemens confirmed to the Guardian.

title: Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies aged 83

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Democratic senator-elect reiterates suggestion to rename Medicare for All after Trump if president allows bill to pass

Michigan US senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday doubled down on naming healthcare reform legislation after Donald Trump as long as it meant the president would not impede its passage.

“If he’s open to the conversation, I am open to it, too,” El-Sayed said of Trump on Sunday. “If the president is opening to signing that bill, let’s get it done.”

description:
Australia’s climate change minister will face a torrent of criticism over his role, but disagreement over fossil fuels proved an unbridgeable sticking point

After delivering a major speech to the UN climate talks in Turkey last week, the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, dismissed criticisms that he hadn’t managed to name the problem that is overwhelming driving catastrophic global heating – burning fossil fuels.

“You could pick out any number of things that were not in what was a short speech,” he later said.

title: Cop31 left Chris Bowen stuck between petrostates and climate reality. But the failure to say the f-word is not his alone

author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday

Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China.

Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and posted a photo of himself and Putin shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”
title: US intelligence chief says he trusts Trump’s description of Putin as ‘my friend’

description:
John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips

Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”.

The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. author: Associated Press
description:
Milestone reached Sunday, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Virginia Foxx in North Carolina

House Democrats have secured their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in a midterm election sweep unseen since 1992 that creates not only vast opportunities to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities.

Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, four more than the 40 they picked up in Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats capture at least 258 House seats in largest sweep since 1992

author: Henry Belot and Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Transparency International says Queensland’s David Crisafulli was ‘by far the most frequently accessed’ state leader, with 13 meetings

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Bosses at 10 datacentre companies secured almost 120 meetings with premiers and ministers in five states over a three-year period, with experts declaring this is “just the tip of the iceberg”.

Analysis by Transparency International Australia argues these meetings, when combined with political donations, demonstrate “unfettered access” to decision-makers that creates an “uneven playing field”.
title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Incoming House speaker says party focused on affordability and fixing ‘broken’ healthcare and immigration systems

The incoming US House speaker, Hakeem Jeffries, has said he and his fellow Democrats are focused on affordability, expanding healthcare and fixing the “broken” immigration system in the country – and willing to cross the political aisle to do so.

Jeffries laid out that agenda in an interview on Sunday with CBS News’s Face the Nation, less than three weeks after Democrats seized control of Congress during the 3 November midterms for the latter half of Donald Trump’s second presidency.

Continue reading...
title: Hakeem Jeffries willing to cross political aisle to work on Democrats’ agenda

author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv, Angelique Chrisafis and agencies
description:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

An explosion on a Russian ship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya’s eastern-based government has said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the suspected strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the frontlines.

Continue reading...
title: Blast on Russian ship in Benghazi a suspected drone attack, say Libyan authorities

author: Peter Walker
description:
Conservatives may instinctively want to push back against closer EU ties, but they have to train their focus elsewhere

Anyone who accidentally switched to BBC One at about 9.45am on Sunday to be greeted by Theresa May awkwardly espousing the virtues of Brexit could have been forgiven for thinking they had woken up in around 2018 – and not being especially pleased at the idea.

This is one of the problems now facing May’s party. For all that it is a reflex action for Conservatives to push back against closer ties with the EU, Andy Burnham’s decision to pursue such a course plunges them back into their own unhappy place.

Continue reading...
title: Theresa May’s blast from the past calls Tories back to their unhappy place | Peter Walker

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Unfolding crisis shows importance of ‘human connections’ over the long term – especially in under-vaccinated areas

Tristan Sharratt, a family nurse practitioner and public health researcher, began serving an Amish community in central New York almost inadvertently. A friend told an Amish neighbor that Sharratt was accepting new patients and was a good, solid guy. Word spread quickly, and now Sharratt sees many members of the community, which numbers in the hundreds.

He is what is called a “trusted messenger” – someone who understands a community and has earned their respect. Other trusted messengers can be neighbors, co-workers, customers, midwives, or people who work as long-distance drivers for the Amish. Connecting with such people will be crucial for ending the measles outbreak and preventing future crises.

Continue reading...
title: Experts say ‘trusted messengers’ critical as Amish grapple with measles outbreak

One serial sweary offender, Jacqui Lambie, says it wouldn’t be an Australian parliament ‘without a few swear words thrown in’

When Liberal MP Garth Hamilton stormed out of parliament in June, slamming his hands on his desk and calling out “fucking bullshit” the speaker of the house, Milton Dick, called it “a new low” in federal politics.

Dick may have been on to something.

title: Australia urged to wean off imported fossil fuels amid global supply shocks

Grammy-winning pop star Miley ⁠Cyrus married her longtime partner, drummer Maxx Morando, ⁠in California on ⁠Saturday, ​People magazine and other US entertainment news outlets ⁠reported.

author: Adria R Walker
description:
More than 120 people in the Tennessee city were detained in one of the largest single-day ICE raids in the US in 2026

The date 1 September, or 9/01 Day, is a festive day for Memphians. The date mirrors the city’s 901 area code, and gives residents a reason to come together to celebrate the city and the people who love it. When 9/01 Day falls on a weekday, as it did this year, the celebration starts the weekend prior, extending the festivities. Groups across the city hosted celebrations featuring food vendors, DJs, musicians and members of the Memphis Grizzlies, the local NBA team, while dozens of local businesses offered $9.01-themed specials.

But for the families of 121 people, this past 1 September will be remembered for a different reason – just days prior, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained their friends and relatives, con
title: They went out to celebrate at a Memphis bar. Then, ICE descended

author: Jeremy Barr in Washington
description:
Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga

As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.

“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.

Continue readi
title: Conservative media weighs its future as cracks emerge in Trump’s movement

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Jay Stewart joined search party after two-year-old Vella Campillo wandered off into desert from front yard of home

An Arizona granddad has been formally recognized as a hero after recently volunteering to help search for a toddler who wandered off alone into the desert while wearing only a diaper – and finding her safely within several hours curled up under a bush, leading to her rescue.

“I’ll never forget it as long as I live,” Jay Stewart said of recovering Vella Campillo, two, while recalling the moment at a news conference held later. “I’ve never wanted to find something so bad in my life – or somebody to find her, anybody to find her.”

Continue reading...
title: Arizona grandfather hailed as a hero after finding missing toddler in desert

It’s not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers’ time, officials’ time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you’re getting out what you want.

Joshua Howard, 31, is believed to have been struck by a car and thrown over the guardrail as he was walking home from a party in Rouse Hill

The twin brother of a man whose body lay undiscovered for 12 days after he was killed in a suspected hit and run in Sydney says it has left him feeling like half a person.

Joshua Howard was last seen at a bus interchange in Parramatta, in western Sydney, about 10pm on 7 November.

author: Petra Stock
description:
State faces electricity supply gap when Yallourn coal-fired power station closes in 2028 as experts warn neither Labor nor the Coalition has adequate plans

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Victoria’s electricity supply will be at risk when a major power plant shuts in 2028 and neither major party is offering a plan at this month’s state election to deal with it, experts have warned.

All parties concede the giant Yallourn coal plant, which has operated in the Latrobe Valley since the 1970s and supplies a fifth of Victoria’s energy, is at the end of its functional life and will shut in less than two years. Analysts say the parties vying to run the state are failing to properly explain how they will fill the power shortfall the closure will cr
title: ‘No time for a culture war’: Victoria’s electricity supply is at risk. Can it avoid power shortages and bill shocks?

description:
Controversial figure frequently took positions against drug use, abortion and homosexuality, but in later years supported legislation expunging homosexual convictions

The former New South Wales MP and longstanding figurehead of the rightwing Christian Democratic party, the Rev Fred Nile, has died aged 92.

Nile was a member of the NSW legislative council for more than 40 years. He first entered the state’s upper house in 1981 and retired after unsuccessfully contesting the 2023 election.
